title: Attention-path prefilter and adaptive windowing for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Continuous batching currently struggles with heterogeneous request shapes and attention-heavy long-context requests. We observe tail-latency spikes when long-prefill sequences are admitted into batches optimized for short-decoding kernels. This ticket introduces an attention-path prefilter stage plus an adaptive windowing policy to improve kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling across mixed workloads.

Goal: Reduce 99th percentile latency for mixed short+long workloads by 20-30% without increasing median token cost by more than 5% and maintain correctness of model outputs. Implement a lightweight prefilter that classifies incoming requests by attention footprint (estimated tokens * attention-scaling factor) and uses a warm-kernel affinity score to decide admission routing (fast small-kernel path vs. large-context kernel path). Combine this with an adaptive sliding window batch shaper that maintains tail fairness using token-budgeted soft deferral and scheduled micro-slices for long-context decodes.

Scope: Engineering implementation in serving runtime admission pipeline, kernel-affinity scoring, integration with KV-cache hinting, new telemetry events, and a canary rollout through dedicated capacity. This work will not change model weights or tokenization.

Non-goals: Full-fledged model-level rewriter, end-to-end cost optimizations across customer billing (follow-ups will analyze pricing impact).
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile end-to-end latency for mixed demo workload reduced by >=20% in canary compared to baseline
Median per-token cost increase <=5% for canary workloads
No regression in top-1 output equality (unit prompt set) beyond existing flakiness thresholds
New telemetry events emitted for kernel-affinity decisions, admission-deferral, and micro-slice scheduling
Canary rollout plan and rollback path documented in the runbook
tasks: Design kernel-affinity scoring (attention footprint, kernel warmth, quantization compatibility, cache-hit probability)
Implement prefilter stage in admission controller with pluggable policy hook
Add adaptive window batch shaper with token-budgeted soft-deferral and micro-slice scheduler
Integrate with KV cache hinting to prefer warmed kernels for sequences with high affinity
Instrument telemetry: decision tags, latency breakdown, kernel-switch frequency
Create e2e benchmark harness (mixed short/long synthetic + sampled customer traces)
Run canary on dedicated pool, collect metrics for two weeks, analyze regressions
If stable, stage rollout to additional Dedicated clusters and then hosted API
design_notes: Affinity score formula draft: affinity = alpha*estimated_attention_ops + beta*(1 - kernel_warmth) + gamma*quant_compat_penalty - delta*cache_hit_estimate. Weights are tunable; initial alpha=1, beta=0.6, gamma=1.2, delta=0.8
Prefilter must execute in <=200us on admission to avoid adding overhead; implement as inline C++/Rust path with fast-path using lookup table for common lengths
Adaptive window uses sliding window of up to N=64 batches; token-budget is computed per-tenant to avoid starvation (soft-defer allows up to T seconds of wait before forced admission)

Micro-slices for long decodes: instead of admitting an entire long prefill into a decode-optimized kernel, schedule it as micro-slices of fixed token chunks to improve packing with short requests and reduce tail spikes
Fallback: if kernel compatibility mismatch or cache coldness detected, fall back to decode-kernel pool with preemptive KV warmup if possible
experiments: A/B: baseline vs prefilter+adaptive-window on synthetic mixed workload (50% short 16-32 tokens, 50% long 1024-2048 tokens)
Kernel-warmth threshold sweep: test warmth thresholds [0.2,0.5,0.8] to find knee for affinity decisions
Soft-defer time budget sweep: evaluate T in [5ms, 20ms, 50ms] for tail-latency vs throughput trade-off
Micro-slice size sweep: evaluate slices of 32, 64, 128 tokens for packing efficiency
observability: Add metrics: admission_route (enum), affinity_score (histogram), deferred_count, micro_slice_count, kernel_switch_count
Tracing: attach decision tags to request trace (kernel_chosen, reason_code, estimated_attention_ops)
Dashboards: P99 latency by admission_route, per-tenant token-budget usage, kernel-warmth heatmap
Alerts: P99 deviation >15% for canary pool, deferred_count > expected baseline by 3x
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Prefilter adds CPU overhead and could increase median latency for ultra-low-latency tenants. Mitigation: fast-path cold-start detection and a config flag to disable prefilter per-tenant.

Risk: Incorrect affinity calculus routes requests to incompatible kernel causing increased decoding errors. Mitigation: explicit compatibility checks and conservative initial thresholds; run compatibility unit tests across model variants.
Risk: Soft-deferral causes starvation for small tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant quota and forced admission after budget exhaustion.
Risk: Increased complexity in rollout and debugging. Mitigation: extensive telemetry, runbook section, and incremental canary rollout with kill-switch
rollout_plan: Unit tests + integration tests in CI (PR link below)
Internal staging run with recorded customer traces (3 days)
Canary on 5% of dedicated capacity for 14 days; automatic rollback criteria defined
Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% in dedicated, then hosted API after 30 days of stable metrics
